pages.title: About Court Vision: a free basketball GM and simulation game
pages.description: Court Vision is a free, browser-based pixel-art basketball management game with real NBA history, a full simulation engine, and seven game modes, from franchise GM to the 82-0 Challenge.
pages.lead: CourtVision is a free browser basketball management and simulation game developed by NineFoldVision. Its focus is letting you explore basketball decisions: build a roster, change a rotation, replay a historical matchup or follow a player’s career, then see how those choices play out possession by possession.

items: **Run a franchise (GM mode).** Draft, trade, negotiate contracts with agents, hire coaches, handle injuries, set rotations and play through the regular season, the In-Season Cup, the trade deadline, the playoffs and the offseason. See [How to Play](how-to-play.html).

**Play real NBA history.** Start a league in any season from 1946-47 to today with real players, real rosters and their real careers, awards and champions. See [Real NBA history](guides/real-nba-history.html).
**League Hunt.** Spin a six-man squad from all of basketball history and win ten best-of-seven series against the great teams of every era. See the [League Hunt guide](guides/league-hunt.html).
**Career Mode.** Create one player and live his entire career, from draft night to the Hall of Fame and the all-time Top 100. See the [Career Mode guide](guides/career-mode.html).
**Rebuild Challenge.** Take over a real team at its lowest point and win a title before time runs out. See the [Rebuild Challenge guide](guides/rebuild-challenge.html).

**82-0 Challenge.** Spin or pick a ten-man team from all of history and try to go 82-0, then 16-0 in the playoffs, against real teams and boss teams like the 72-10 Bulls. See the [82-0 Challenge guide](guides/82-0-challenge.html).
**All-Time Draft.** Thirty teams, thirteen rounds, every player in history at his best: draft against AI GMs, then play the season. See the [All-Time Draft guide](guides/all-time-draft.html).
**Survival.** Keep a team competitive while defeated opponents claim players from your roster. Protect your Franchise Player and decide when to spend shields.
**Story Mode.** Follow Street to the League through basketball games, characters and decisions.
**Your Career.** Begin at age 13 and choose a route through youth basketball and professional opportunities. Compare all seven main modes in the [FAQ](faq.html).

blocks.text: Every game is simulated play by play. Players have more than seventy ratings (shooting from every zone, finishing, passing, defense, rebounding, athleticism, basketball IQ and more) and tendencies that decide what they try to do. Coaches set pace, three-point frequency, defensive schemes and rotations. The engine is calibrated against real NBA league averages for pace, shooting, fouls and assists, so box scores look like real box scores.

You can watch any game on a pixel-art court, coach it live from the sideline (timeouts, play calls, double teams, last-shot plays), or simulate whole seasons in seconds. Simulation runs in background workers, so the game stays responsive while a season plays out.

Local leagues and in-progress Career Mode worlds stay in your browser. An optional account syncs supported profile progress and retired Career Mode records; it is not a full league backup. Download a backup from the GM Locker or Backups before moving devices or clearing browser data. The [FAQ](faq.html) explains recovery, and the [Privacy Policy](privacy.html) describes storage and advertising.
You can also install Court Vision as an app on your PC or phone: it gets its own icon and window and plays offline. Open [courtvisiongame.com/#/install](./#/install) for the steps.

The built-in NBA history (statistics, awards and drafts) comes from [Basketball-Reference.com](https://www.basketball-reference.com/), compiled by Sumitro Datta in the [bball-reference-datasets](https://github.com/sumitrodatta/bball-reference-datasets) project. Champions, Finals MVPs, All-Star Game MVPs and Coaches of the Year come from [NBA.com](https://www.nba.com/news/history-all-time-awards). Player ratings, skill attributes and team names are Court Vision's own, computed from the statistics.
Court Vision is an independent fan project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the NBA, its teams, its players or these data sources.
Share your leagues and careers, report bugs and suggest features on our [Discord server](https://discord.gg/5uGK5HDS8e). New features ship regularly; see the [changelog](changelog.html).

pages.title: How to play Court Vision: a beginner's guide to running a franchise
pages.description: Start your first Court Vision league: choosing a team, setting a rotation, the season calendar, trades, the draft, free agency and the offseason.
pages.lead: This guide walks you through your first season as general manager, from picking a team to your first offseason. Everything here applies to both random leagues and real NBA history leagues.

items: On the main menu, choose **Franchise**, then select a generated league, a real historical league or one of the available challenge setups.
Pick a trade difficulty. **Normal** means trades need roughly matched value; **Hard** puts a premium on young high-potential players.
Choose a team to run, or create an expansion team through a real expansion draft where every club files a protection list first.
Pick **Simple** navigation for a guided sidebar, or **Full** to see every page. You can switch any time.

blocks.text: Open **Roster** to order your depth chart: the first five are starters. Minutes targets decide who plays how much. Players who get fewer minutes than they expect lose morale and some ask to be traded, so give your best players the minutes they have earned.

Your head coach's system (pace, three-point frequency, defensive scheme) shapes how the team plays. The **Coaching** page lets you adjust tendencies; the coaching staff also affects player development.
Use the **Play** button to simulate a day, a week, to the next event or the rest of the season. The season stops for the big moments:

items: **In-Season Cup:** group games, a knockout bracket and a final you can watch.
**All-Star Weekend:** captains draft their teams, plus the three-point contest, dunk contest and Rising Stars.
**Trade Deadline Day:** a 9 AM to 3 PM clock, a rumor mill, AI teams calling with offers, and deals breaking all day.
**Playoffs:** a play-in, four rounds, and your series live if you want to watch.
**Trades.** Build an offer and the AI front office answers, often with a counteroffer instead of a flat no. Three-team trades are possible too.
**Free agency.** Players weigh money, role, winning and loyalty. Negotiate through their agents; a player who walks away will not sign with you that offseason.
**Contracts.** Extend players during the season before they reach free agency. Watch the salary cap and the luxury tax on the Finances page.
**Medical room.** When a player is hurt, the doctors ask for a call: rest him longer or bring him back early at a risk.

blocks.text: After the Finals come the awards, the Draft Lottery and Draft Night, where you can trade picks in the war room. Summer League follows, then re-signings, then free agency. Players age and develop over the summer: young players with minutes and good coaching grow the most. Your owner reviews your season against the goals set before it, and your job security depends on it.

items: Check **Power Rankings** and **Standings** before trading: know whether you are a contender or a seller.
A young player's **Potential** is his ceiling; minutes and coaching decide how close he gets.
Use **Auto Play** to simulate several seasons at once when you want to see a rebuild through.
Back up your progress now and then from the main menu (Backups) or the GM Locker.

blocks.text: Pick **All-Time Draft** on the main menu, choose your franchise, your draft slot (or a random one) and the era whose rules the season is played under. Thirty teams then draft in snake order for thirteen rounds from every player in NBA history, each at his best season. The table shows every player's rating, best season and, for the all-time greats, their place in the all-time Top 100; filter by guards, forwards or bigs, or search a name.

AI GMs take the best player left for what their roster still needs, so bigs and guards run out as the rounds go on. **Best fit** suggests your pick, and **Auto-draft the rest** finishes for you. When the draft is done you see where your team ranks on paper; then the season starts in a normal GM league: trades, free agency, the draft, and as many seasons as you like, with players aging and developing from their best years.

pages.title: Career Mode guide: the wheel, MyPlayer, training and the all-time Top 100
pages.description: How Career Mode works in Court Vision: building a player on the wheel of NBA history or in MyPlayer, development, free agency, awards, the Hall of Fame and the Top 100.
pages.lead: In Career Mode you create one player and live his whole career, season by season, in a real league played by the full simulation engine. At the end you see where he ranks among the greatest players of all time.

sections.h2: Choose when he enters the league

blocks.text: Start in today's league (the 2026 draft) or pick any past draft from 1947 to 2025. In a past draft the league is real NBA history from the season before: real rosters, real players on their real careers, and the real draft class. Enter the 1984 draft and you share the stage with Michael Jordan, Hakeem Olajuwon and Charles Barkley.

Every real player in NBA history sits on the wheel once, at his best season. The odds lean a little toward good players: a Star comes up about 7% of the time and a Great about 18%. When the wheel stops you take one of that player's ten categories, and your player gets his exact ratings in it.

rows: weight, strength, balance, stamina and durability
layups, dunks, touch and the post
mid-range, long twos and free throws
basketball IQ, clutch, composure and consistency

blocks.text: Tools: **Move Left** and **Move Right** shift a stopped wheel by one slice (once each), two **Respins** spin again without taking anything, and one **Triple Spin** spins three wheels at once so you can take a category from each.

The best ever at a skill go past 99. The top 60 in each skill, ranked by what they actually did that season (threes made, assists, steals, rebounds and blocks, efficient scoring), carry up to +21, so the very best reach 120. Take Stephen Curry's shooting and your player shoots like the best shooter ever. On the court, points above 99 count half, so a 120 shooter is the greatest ever, not a 70% three-point shooter.

Set height, weight and wingspan, then spend a budget of points across nine skills. Height sets the limits: a seven-footer cannot handle like a point guard and a small guard cannot protect the rim like a center. You also choose how ready he is: a late bloomer starts further from his prime but peaks higher; an NBA-ready rookie starts close to it.

items: **Draft night.** Where he goes depends on his rating and potential against the rest of the class.
**Training focus.** Each summer pick two categories. They grow faster, and training can carry them past his prime. Everything grows quickly when he is young and declines with age, athleticism first.
**Free agency.** When his contract runs out he gets offers: the biggest contract, a title contender, the biggest role, or his old team.
**Trade requests.** Ask out to a contender, for a bigger role, or anywhere but here.
**Autopilot.** Let the game make sensible choices for the rest of his career; take control back whenever you like.

blocks.text: Each season shows his stats, his team's record and playoff run, every award, and the moments of his year: his first 40-point game, his first triple-double, 20,000 career points.

sections.h2: Legacy, the Hall of Fame and the Top 100

blocks.text: When he retires you get his full career: totals, per-game averages, a pixel trophy shelf, his Overall by age, and any team that retires his number (five seasons there plus three All-Star years, a title or an MVP). His **Legacy Score** decides the Hall of Fame (45 gets him in, 90 makes him a first-ballot pick) and his place on the all-time Top 100. The [Ratings explained](guides/ratings-explained.html) guide shows how the score is built.
Your Hall of Famers get plaques in the Career Mode Hall of Fame and in the GM Locker. A retired or active player can also be brought into any GM league from the Free Agency page.

After a season with something special in it (a title, an MVP, a 50-point night, a first All-Star selection, a playoff exit, the rookie wall, or the first signs of Father Time) you make a call. Every answer is worth something: **Legacy Score** right away, or a summer of extra work in one skill that shows up in your ratings next season. Your calls appear in the career timeline. On autopilot, seasons play on without them.

pages.title: League Hunt guide: spins, series, boosts, the shop and the Daily Legend
pages.description: How League Hunt works in Court Vision: spinning a six-man squad from basketball history, era rules, best-of-seven series, boosts, shops, difficulty and the Daily Legend.
pages.lead: League Hunt is a quick run through basketball history. Build a six-man squad and a coach from any era, then win ten best-of-seven series against real teams, each played under the rules of its time.

blocks.text: The draft is a slot machine with seven reels: point guard, shooting guard, small forward, power forward, center, sixth man (any position) and coach. They all spin at once; you hit STOP, lock one of the seven, and the rest spin again, until every slot is locked. Cards are player-seasons, so 1996 Michael Jordan and 2003 Michael Jordan are different cards. Early rounds are richer than late ones, and one early round always lands a Star on the reels, another a Great.
Coaches add from -2 to +5 overall to everyone and bring a style: defense, pace, threes or ball movement. A coach also adds a point of chemistry for players from a franchise he won with.

Every team, yours included, has a rating from its best six players with the star weighted most. The scale follows real results: 60 is a bad team, 70 about 40 wins, 80 about 45, 90 a 55 to 62 win team, and 100 a 68-win all-time great. More in [Ratings explained](guides/ratings-explained.html).

items: Ten best-of-seven series against real teams, each played under its era's rules: no three-point line before 1979-80, hand-checking in the 1990s, the pace of the time.
Series 5 is a semi-boss and series 10 is the boss, one of the best teams ever, rated 100.
From series 2 on, teams bring buffs such as Superstar Takeover, Hostile Crowd or Playoff Veterans. Bosses bring more, and stronger ones.
Losing a series costs a life, and you replay it.

sections.h2: Boosts, the shop and your focus

blocks.text: After a series win you pick one of three boosts; a hunt holds three. Many grow inside a series: the Sixth Man Spark adds +3 to your sixth man for every game you have won in it. Boosts add at most +6 to one player in one game.

A shop comes before series 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9: players for a specific slot, a better coach, items that last the whole hunt, and training. Lives are for sale only on Rookie. You also pick what the team works on: developing the star, developing the sixth man, team chemistry, or the coach's system.

sections.h2: Decks, difficulty and the Daily Legend

items: **Decks** change how the draft opens: Big Man Era, Old School (pre-1980 players only), Pace & Space (2010 on) and Dynasty. They unlock as you play.
**Difficulty:** Rookie (softer teams, four lives), Pro, and Legend (tougher teams, two lives, a top-four all-time boss).
**Daily Legend:** one hunt a day, the same for everyone. Keep your streak going.
**Album:** every card you have had on a squad, with progress toward each era's stars.
**Dream Matchup:** play any two real team-seasons against each other under any era's rules.

pages.title: 82-0 Challenge guide: Quick Spin, Franchise Spin, bosses and scoring
pages.description: How the 82-0 Challenge works in Court Vision: building a ten-man team from NBA history, Quick Spin and Franchise Spin, boss teams, lineup rules, chemistry, scoring, the Daily 82-0 and rewards.
pages.lead: The 82-0 Challenge asks one question: can your team go undefeated? Build a ten-man team and a coach from all of NBA history, play a full 82-game season against real teams from every era, then four best-of-seven playoff rounds. The goal is 82-0, then 16-0.

items: **Quick Spin:** ten spins (point guard, shooting guard, small forward, power forward and center, then five bench spots) and a coach spin. Whatever the reel lands on is yours. Fast and full of luck.

**Franchise Spin:** each spin rolls a franchise and an era, for example the Warriors in the 2010s. You see everyone who played there in that era, each at his best season with the team, and pick **one**. You get one team reroll, one era reroll and one **Absolute Prime** boost, which shows that spin's players at the best season of their whole career. More choice, tougher opponents.
**From League Hunt:** after you win a hunt, you can take that six-man squad and its coach into an 82-0 season, plus four bench spins. Hunt squads have their own record.

blocks.text: The 82 games are against real team-seasons, getting tougher as the season goes on, and every game is played under the rules of the opponent's era. Six boss teams sit on the schedule: Wilt's 68-13 Sixers, the 1971-72 Lakers who won 33 straight, Bird's 1985-86 Celtics, the 72-10 Bulls, the 73-9 Warriors and the 2016-17 Warriors. The playoffs are four best-of-seven rounds against stronger and stronger teams, ending with a champion.
You can play one game at a time, or sim the season and watch the record tick up. A banner tracks whether 82-0 is still alive, and when the streak breaks it shows the game and the team that did it.

items: Your five best players start. If no guard starts, or no big man (center or power forward) starts, the starters play worse. Three starters at one position also costs a little.
Real teammates from the same season, players from the same franchise and famous rivals on the same side play better together.
Ratings are ranked within each season, so a 1965 star and a 2016 star stand on the same scale. See [Ratings explained](guides/ratings-explained.html).

rows: 100, plus the winning margin up to 25

items: **Daily 82-0:** the same spins for everyone each day, alternating between Quick Spin and Franchise Spin. Your best try of the day counts, and your best day of the week goes on the online weekly board.

**Rewards:** the Undefeated title and profile frame for an 82-0 season, and the gold Perfection title and frame for 98-0 (82-0 and 16-0). Five achievements and Trophy Road points for your best season, titles and perfect seasons.
**Share cards:** a landscape card or a 9:16 card for TikTok and Stories, with your whole season as a strip of wins and losses.

pages.title: All-Time Draft guide: thirty teams, thirteen rounds, every player at his best
pages.description: How the All-Time Draft works in Court Vision: thirty teams draft every player in NBA history at his best season, AI GMs who draft for need, and a full season under any era's rules.
pages.lead: The All-Time Draft puts every player in NBA history into one draft pool, each at his best season. Thirty teams take turns for thirteen rounds; you draft against AI GMs, then play a full season with the whole GM game.

items: Thirty teams, thirteen rounds: a full roster for everyone.
Every player in history is in the pool at his best season, so the first picks are the greatest players ever.
AI GMs draft for need: a team with three guards goes looking for a big man. A draft board shows every pick, the clock, and the steals and reaches.

blocks.text: Your drafted team plays a full season in the GM game, under the rules of the era you choose: trades, rotations, coaching, the playoffs. Titles count toward your GM legacy and achievements.
Every week there is a shared All-Time Draft with the same order, era and AI GMs for everyone, so you can compare drafts with friends.

items: Take the best player available early, then fill positions: a team needs someone to bring the ball up and someone to protect the rim.
Late rounds are where role players win titles: shooters and defenders matter more than names.
Learn how player ratings compare across eras in [Ratings explained](guides/ratings-explained.html).

pages.title: Rebuild Challenge guide: scenarios, scoring and stars
pages.description: How the Rebuild Challenge works in Court Vision: take over a real NBA team at its lowest point and win a championship before the clock runs out.
pages.lead: Take over a real team at the lowest point in its history and win a championship before time runs out. The league is real NBA history from that season, and you run the team with every tool of the full game.

blocks.text: You start with the real roster of that season. Around you, real players follow their real careers and real draft classes arrive each year, so the 2003 class still holds LeBron James and the 1984 class Michael Jordan, but where they land depends on the lottery and on you. Trades, free agency, the draft and coaching all work as in the main game.

Every Monday at 00:00 UTC a new Rebuild of the Week starts on the main menu. It picks one scenario and one twist, and builds the league from a seed shared by everyone, so every player starts from the same rosters, the same draft classes and the same generated players. Your best score of the week is kept in this browser; post your share card on Discord to compare.

items: **Standard rules:** the scenario as written.
**Short clock:** one season less than usual.
**Tough GMs:** trades need tightly matched value.
**Short clock, tough GMs:** both at once.
Every season scores 2 points per win plus a playoff bonus: 20 for the first round, 40 for the second, 70 for the conference finals, 120 for the Finals.
A title scores 1,000 plus 250 for every season you had left.
Stars: one for making the playoffs, two for reaching the Finals, three for winning it all.
If you are fired, the challenge ends. Leagues where Sandbox or God Mode was used do not go on the board.

blocks.text: Your best score, stars and fastest title for each scenario show in the scenario picker and in the GM Locker.

items: Short scenarios reward buying veterans early; long ones reward stacking picks and young players.
Cap space is the fastest route to a star, but free agents weigh winning: a team with no hope rarely lands the best ones.
Keep your owner happy: missing the season goals badly can cost you the job before the clock runs out.

pages.title: Real NBA history in Court Vision: start any season since 1946
pages.description: How Court Vision's Real League works: real rosters from any season since 1946-47, real careers, real draft classes, ratings computed from statistics, and Real Player Development.
pages.lead: Real League starts from actual NBA history: pick any season from 1946-47 to today and take over a real team with its real roster, in a league that already holds every past season's stats, awards and champions.

items: Every player's year-by-year statistics, awards, All-Star selections and draft position up to your starting season.
Rosters reconstructed from that season's real participation, with real jersey numbers.
Real mid-season trades and the real draft classes of the coming years (optional).
An option to load every real player, so players who retired before your start still have their careers and profiles.

blocks.text: Court Vision computes every player's ratings from his statistics: each season's players are ranked by production and given the Overall spread of a generated league, and skill attributes are estimated from his shooting, rebounding, passing and defensive numbers. The ratings are Court Vision's own; they are not official and not taken from any other game.

With Real Player Development on, real players follow their real careers: a rookie Jordan becomes the Jordan of 1991 on schedule, and players decline and retire when they really did. Players you create, draft from generated classes or import grow through Court Vision's own development. Turn it off to let every career go its own way.

items: **1984-85:** the Jordan, Hakeem and Barkley rookie class.
**1996-97:** Kobe, Iverson and Nash arrive; the Bulls are at their peak.
**2003-04:** LeBron, Wade, Melo and Bosh enter the league.
**2014-15:** the Warriors' first title season and the dawn of the three-point era.

pages.title: Ratings explained: Overall, team rating, Legacy Score and the Top 100
pages.description: How Court Vision rates players and teams: player Overall, the 0-100 team rating matched to real win totals, ratings past 99, the Legacy Score and the all-time Top 100.
pages.lead: Court Vision uses a few different numbers. This page explains what each one means and how it is built.

blocks.text: Overall is a weighted summary of a player's most important ratings for his position: shooting, finishing, playmaking, defense, rebounding and athleticism. It is a quick guide, not the whole story: the engine uses every individual rating and tendency, so two 75-rated players can play very differently.

League Hunt rates teams from their best six players, weighted from the top (25%, 21%, 18%, 15%, 12%, 9%), because one great player is worth more than two good ones. That weighted strength is lined up against the real distribution of win totals across every team-season in NBA history, then turned into a rating:
No real team goes past 100, but a squad built in League Hunt can.

In Career Mode, the top 60 players ever at a skill carry ratings past 99, up to 120, ranked by what they really did: threes made (Stephen Curry), assists (John Stockton, Steve Nash), steals, rebounds and blocks (Wilt Chamberlain, Dikembe Mutombo). In games, every point past 99 counts half.
The Legacy Score measures a whole career. It is computed the same way for real players (from the NBA history data) and for players you create:
A Legacy Score of 45 puts a player in the Hall of Fame; 90 makes him a first-ballot pick.

The Top 100 is a fixed, hand-ordered list: LeBron James is 1, Michael Jordan 2, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar 3, Tim Duncan 4, Stephen Curry 7 and Kobe Bryant 12. A created player's place on it is one plus the number of listed players whose Legacy Score is higher than his.

pages.title: CourtVision FAQ: game modes, saves, accounts and troubleshooting
pages.description: Learn how to play CourtVision, choose between seven basketball simulation modes, understand ratings and relics, back up saves, and manage accounts and privacy.
pages.lead: Choose a topic or search for a question. These answers explain the game available now, from your first franchise to protecting a long-running save. For a step-by-step franchise walkthrough, read [How to Play](how-to-play.html).

blocks.text: CourtVision is a basketball management and simulation game by NineFoldVision. You make roster, training and coaching decisions, then the simulation plays out possessions and produces results. You can run a franchise, build historical teams for short challenges, or follow one player through a career. Pixel-art games let you watch the action as well as read the statistics.

Yes. You can play the browser game for free. The web version includes advertising support and an optional Support Shop with passes and supporter bundles; buying something is not required to start playing. Ad availability depends on your settings, connection and whether an ad is served.

Open the game and choose a mode on the main menu. Choose **Franchise** for a league you manage over multiple seasons; its setup includes real historical leagues, generated leagues and challenges. Choose **82-0 Challenge** for a focused team-building run, or **Career Mode** to follow one player. Read the setup rules before starting: each mode has its own goals and options.

For your first franchise, pick a team, inspect its roster, set a rotation and simulate a game before advancing a whole season. The [beginner guide](how-to-play.html) walks through trades, the schedule and the offseason.

No account is required for local single-player play. An optional account enables cloud progress and online features such as posting results and maintaining a public profile. Those features require an internet connection and an available account service; they are not the same as local saves.

sections.h2: Can I play on my phone?

blocks.text: The game includes mobile layouts and runs in modern phone browsers. Large roster tables may need horizontal scrolling, and longer simulations can take more time on a phone. Try a short challenge first, keep the tab open while it runs, and use a larger screen when you want more room for detailed management.
If Google sign-in fails inside Instagram or another in-app browser, open CourtVision in your normal browser and start sign-in there.

No. The browser version starts from the website. Installation is optional: the [installation guide](./#/install) explains adding the app to supported devices. A Windows download is also linked there. Your browser and the installed edition may keep separate local saves, so use a backup when moving between them.

sections.h2: What game modes are there, and how long do they take?

blocks.text: The seven main menu choices are **Franchise, League Hunt, 82-0 Challenge, Career Mode, Survival, Story Mode and Your Career**. Franchise includes additional setups such as Rebuild Challenge and All-Time Draft. Some modes offer daily, weekly or difficulty variants.

Short challenges can fit a brief session, while franchise management can continue for many seasons. Actual time depends on your device, how much you watch and how many decisions you make; menu time estimates are not limits.

Manage a team across the season and offseason: set rotations, hire staff, trade, negotiate contracts, scout prospects and draft. Real historical setups and generated leagues offer different starting points. Budgets, roster needs and player development make a strong team a longer-term project than simply collecting high overall ratings.

The Franchise setup also includes Rebuild Challenge, All-Time Draft, Time Machine and World Games options. Check each setup for its rules. Start with [How to Play](how-to-play.html), then use the [guides](guides/) for a particular challenge.

In **League Hunt**, spin a six-player squad and a coach, lock your choices, and choose a training focus. The standard road contains ten best-of-seven series under historical era rules, with a semi-boss and a final boss. Between series you choose boosts and visit shops at designated stops.

Losing a series costs a life; the starting number depends on difficulty. Spend resources with the next matchup in mind, rather than only raising one star’s rating. Special variants and bonus opponents can change the run. See the [League Hunt guide](guides/league-hunt.html).

Build a ten-player team and choose a coach, then try to win all 82 regular-season games and go 16-0 in the playoffs. Setup choices include quick spins, franchise-and-era selections and category-based drafting. A team of scorers still needs defense, rebounding and a workable rotation.
Daily and other variants have their own setup rules. Results and records let you compare runs even when you fall short of perfection. Read the [82-0 guide](guides/82-0-challenge.html).

Create a player through the historical-player wheel or the MyPlayer builder, then follow his seasons, training, team changes, awards and retirement. Wheel choices combine different aspects of real players into your created player; they do not copy one historical career exactly.

Career Mode summarizes a whole playing career and evaluates its legacy. It is separate from **Your Career**, which starts younger and focuses on season-by-season life and basketball choices. See the [Career Mode guide](guides/career-mode.html).

sections.h2: How does Your Career Mode work?

blocks.text: Start a player at age 13 and choose his identity, position and playing style. Decisions shape training and the route through youth basketball, school, college and professional opportunities. Later choices include entering the draft and selecting contracts.
Read the options each season: this mode is about shaping a path over time, rather than using the Career Mode wheel to assemble a finished starting build.

Choose ten players from the opening deal and designate a Franchise Player who cannot be taken. Play historical opponents one game at a time. After a win, the opponent can claim one of your strongest players and you choose a replacement from its offers. Difficulty changes which players are at risk.

Shields protect against player claims; they do not normally erase a lost game. A loss ends the run. Boss opponents appear every fifth round, so saving a shield and maintaining a balanced rotation matter. The Daily Survival uses a shared seed and disables relic bonuses.

**Street to the League** follows a basketball story from the park toward a professional career. Story cards, relationships and decisions connect the games, with different endings depending on the path you take. Games use the simulation engine, while the story gives those results a narrative setting.
Choose Story Mode when you want characters and choices alongside basketball, rather than full control of an entire franchise.

sections.h2: How do player ratings and attributes work?

blocks.text: Overall is a summary, not a guarantee of performance. Individual shooting, finishing, passing, defense, rebounding and physical attributes describe different skills. Tendencies influence what a player attempts, while roles, minutes, teammates and opponents affect the opportunities he gets.

Compare attributes relevant to your lineup: a shooter needs spacing and touches; a defensive big can help without leading the scoring. Rating scales and caps differ between modes and special options. The [ratings guide](guides/ratings-explained.html) explains the main summaries.

sections.h2: How do historical basketball eras work?

blocks.text: Historical franchise setups start with teams and players from the selected season. Era settings and historical challenge matchups can change rules and styles, including three-point availability, pace and defensive conditions. A modern shooting lineup therefore does not play every historical matchup under today’s conditions.

Historical statistics supply inputs, but CourtVision’s ratings and simulated outcomes are its own model. A replay is not a promise to reproduce real standings or careers. Read [Real NBA history](guides/real-nba-history.html).

sections.h2: How do draft classes and scouting work?

blocks.text: Franchise drafts let you compare prospects and use scouting information before making a selection. Historical and generated setups provide different prospect pools. Scout estimates of potential are not certain forecasts: current ability, development and your team’s needs all matter.

Inspect the available reports and player details, compare prospects at the positions you need, and keep more than one target in mind before your pick. The highest estimated potential is not automatically the best immediate starter.

Players change over seasons rather than remaining fixed at their starting rating. Age, potential and development systems affect their progression; training choices let you emphasize aspects of a player’s game. Historical development settings can also influence how real players progress.
Use the player’s current skills and role when choosing training. A promising prospect still needs time, and an older star may decline. The outcome is a simulation, not a guaranteed growth schedule.

sections.h2: Can I watch games and coach?

blocks.text: Yes. The game supports simulated results and a pixel-art Watch Game view. Coaching controls include rotations and tactical decisions; the available controls depend on the mode and screen. Team construction and coaching influence the simulation, but do not guarantee the result of an individual possession.
For franchise management, review the box score as well as the result. Shooting efficiency, turnovers, rebounds and playing time can help explain why a higher-rated roster lost.

Sandbox provides editing tools for experimenting with a league, including player editing and importing historical players. It changes the competitive context: leagues marked as using Sandbox do not qualify for the normal GM achievement and Rebuild Challenge checks. Keep a separate save if you want both an experiment and a competitive franchise.

sections.h2: How do relics and rarity work?

blocks.text: The Relic Vault contains Common, Rare, Epic, Legendary and Mythic relics, plus Secret relics with special abilities. Regular relics contribute luck when equipped in available slots. Duplicate rewards, stacking, upgrades and extra slots are handled by the Vault; simply owning every relic does not equip them all.

Earned rewards and coins can supply more spins. Read the Vault’s current descriptions and odds before spending coins. Shared daily and weekly challenges can disable luck and special abilities to keep their starting conditions comparable.

In the Relic Vault, Lucky Spins use a different rarity distribution and exclude Common relics. They can use earned Lucky Spins or the displayed coin price. They improve the distribution; they do not make every result a Mythic or Secret.

The Career wheel also uses the phrase Lucky Spin for its own player-building mechanic. Follow the explanation on the screen you are using: a Vault spin rewards a relic, while a Career wheel choice affects your player build.

Your profile accumulates XP from supported completed activities and achievements across modes. Level and achievement rewards include progression and cosmetic unlocks, which you can inspect in the profile and GM Locker. The game checks eligibility, so not every edited or experimental result earns competitive progress.

sections.h2: What is the Mode of the Week?

blocks.text: The menu highlights a featured mode that earns bonus XP. Check the current featured-mode panel before starting a run, because the selection rotates and reward limits apply. Daily goals and achievements offer other objectives when you want something more specific than another season.

Community boards compare supported results, profile progression and other records. Sign in to associate online submissions with your account. Different boards measure different things: XP, a career legacy score and a challenge result are not interchangeable rankings.
Shared challenges use their own seeds and eligibility rules. A result must sync successfully before it can appear online; a local record alone does not prove that the server received it.

sections.h2: Where are my saves? Can I lose them?

blocks.text: Leagues and in-progress Career Mode worlds are stored locally in the browser, using browser databases and local storage. Clearing site data, using private browsing, changing browser profiles or switching devices can make those saves unavailable.

An account syncs supported profile progress and retired Career Mode records, not a full copy of every league. Use **Backup everything** in Backups or the GM Locker to download a separate file. A successful cloud sync is not a replacement for a league backup.

Online Leagues are an explicit exception: they share league snapshots through the server. Your Career also syncs its player progress with an account. These features do not turn every local franchise save into a cloud backup.

sections.h2: How do I move my progress to another device?

blocks.text: Download **Backup everything** on the original device. Open CourtVision on the destination device and choose **Restore from a file**. Read the confirmation before restoring: matching records can be replaced, while other records remain. Back up the destination device first if it has progress you want to preserve.

Account sign-in can bring supported synced progress across devices, but active leagues and in-progress Career Mode worlds require a backup. Authentication sessions and account passes are not transferred as ordinary backup data.

sections.h2: What should I do if the game crashes?

blocks.text: First reopen CourtVision in the same browser and profile, then check your saved games. Do not clear site data as a first troubleshooting step: that can delete the local save you are trying to recover. A crash before a save completes may lose recent actions.

For a franchise, check the save recovery controls for available restore points. **Restore as New League** opens a separate recovered save. A downloaded backup is another option. Recovery is only possible if a usable save, restore point or backup exists.

sections.h2: Why does a simulated season take a few seconds?

blocks.text: A season involves many games, each with possessions and player statistics, plus league updates and offseason work. Larger leagues and longer careers require more calculation. The game uses background workers for simulation jobs, but device speed, memory and browser limits still affect completion time.
Keep the tab open while a job runs and avoid repeatedly starting the same action. If it appears stuck, note the mode, season, action and any error message before reopening the game or reporting it.

The installed web app can reuse cached files, and the Windows edition is designed for offline play. Open the modes you need while connected first; cached data can be missing or cleared, so offline availability is not guaranteed for every first-time action.
Signing in, cloud sync, online boards and other server-backed features need a connection. Keep a local backup before relying on offline play or switching editions.

sections.h2: I found a bug or have an idea

blocks.text: Use the [Contact and support page](contact.html) to reach the existing Discord community. Include your mode, browser, device, what you expected, what happened and the steps that trigger it. A screenshot of an error can help.

Do not post passwords, sign-in links or account tokens. Backup files contain your game data; share one only when needed for diagnosis and after checking what it includes. For recovery steps, see the crash and saving answers above.

The web game supports optional Google or Discord sign-in through Supabase Auth. CourtVision uses the provider’s sign-in flow instead of asking you to create a separate game password. A session is kept in your browser so you can stay signed in.

Choose your GM name and check the account’s sync status when moving between devices. On a shared computer, take care which account is signed in: switching accounts can replace the local set of synced profile progress with the other account’s progress.

sections.h2: What information is stored with my account?

blocks.text: The account system uses an account identifier, email and provider details, a GM profile, and supported game progress. Public profiles and boards display information such as your GM name, level, statistics and submitted results. Retired created players can also be public.

Local league saves are separate from cloud profile progress. Optional online features and purchases can process additional records. Read the [Privacy Policy](privacy.html) for the current disclosures, and avoid putting private information in your public GM name.

If you deliberately create or join an Online League, its shared league state is uploaded to Supabase storage so other members can play it. That is separate from ordinary single-player franchise saves. Your Career also includes account-synced player progress; this differs from an in-progress Career Mode world.

sections.h2: Can I delete my account or request help with my data?

blocks.text: The account screen in Community includes account deletion. It calls the server to delete the account; wait for confirmation rather than assuming a failed request worked. Local progress is separate and is not erased just by deleting the account.

If you have a recurring Support Shop pass, cancel the subscription first: deleting a game account is not the same as cancelling billing. For a privacy request or a deletion problem, use [Contact and support](contact.html).

sections.h2: How are cookies and browser storage used?

blocks.text: The game uses local storage and browser databases for saves, settings and account-related state. Google advertising can use cookies or similar technologies. The web version also integrates host analytics and Umami for usage measurements; these are distinct from saving a league.

Open **Cookie Settings** in the game to revisit the configured advertising consent options. Existing third-party cookies may need to be removed using browser controls. Clearing all site data also removes local game progress, so download a backup first. See the [Privacy Policy](privacy.html).

The web version is configured for Google AdSense banner placements. Whether an ad appears depends on consent handling, ad availability, connection, blockers and any active ad-free entitlement. Advertising does not need to load for local gameplay to work. The offline Windows build excludes network ads.
Google’s regional consent message is managed through the site’s advertising configuration. Read the [Privacy Policy](privacy.html) and use the game’s Cookie Settings for your available choices.

sections.h2: Is Court Vision affiliated with the NBA?

blocks.text: No. CourtVision is an independent game by NineFoldVision, not an official NBA product and not endorsed by the NBA, its teams or players. The [About page](about.html) identifies the historical data sources and distinguishes those statistics from the game’s own ratings and simulation.

sections.h2: Can I play the same league as a friend?

blocks.text: A league code lets a friend start from the same league setup while playing a separate simulation. Online Leagues are a different feature: signed-in members share a league state through the server. Check the relevant setup and account status before choosing between a parallel challenge and a shared league.

sections.h2: How do ranked seasons and PvP work?

blocks.text: Ranked competition and League Hunt PvP are available through the online community features. Ranked events contribute points under their own rules; Hunt PvP uses a submitted squad against other players’ teams and tracks a rating. These features require account services and differ from a local single-player run. Check the current event and submission screens for eligibility and results.

pages.title: Court Vision changelog: new game modes and features
pages.description: What's new in Court Vision: the 82-0 Challenge, Mode of the Week, Career Mode big moments, the All-Time Draft, League Hunt and more.
pages.lead: The biggest recent additions to Court Vision, newest first.

items: **82-0 Challenge:** a new mode. Build a ten-man team (Quick Spin or Franchise Spin), play all 82 games against real teams and boss teams like the 72-10 Bulls, then four playoff rounds. Scored runs, a Daily 82-0 with a weekly board, and the Undefeated and Perfection rewards.
**Hunt squads to 82-0:** after you win a League Hunt, take that squad into an 82-0 season as a bonus run.
**Mode of the Week:** one mode earns double XP every week.
**Career Mode big moments:** titles, MVPs, 50-point nights, playoff heartbreak and more now ask you to make a call, worth Legacy or a summer of training.
**Share cards in 9:16** for TikTok, Reels and Stories, with your 82-game season as a strip of wins and losses.
**Menu:** every mode card shows how long a sitting takes, tags, the most popular and most fun picks, and what you have in progress.
**Profile frames, a free Season Pass, a daily streak, your character on the leaderboards** and the Weekly Hunt arrived in the weeks before.
**06 / DRAFT, the All-Time Draft:** thirty teams, thirteen rounds, every player in history at his best season. AI GMs draft for need; your team then plays under any era's rules with the full GM game.
**All-Time Draft of the Week:** the same order, era and AI GMs for everyone.
**Sign in** is now on the main menu.
**Accounts (optional):** sign in with Discord or Google; your progress follows you to every device.
**Community:** leaderboards for GMs, created players (all-time and weekly), the Rebuild and Career of the Week, the Daily Legend, every Rebuild scenario, and your friends.
**Public profiles** with trophies, best created players, achievements (with how rare each one is) and a follow button.
**Ranked seasons:** monthly, with tiers from Bronze to Legend and titles to unlock.
**League Hunt PvP:** your finished hunt squad against other GMs' squads, best of seven, Elo-rated.
**League-code boards:** everyone who played the same league code, and how their first season went.

sections.h2: End of September 2026: levels, goals and leaderboards

items: **GM Profile:** one level across every mode, built from everything you have already done. Levels unlock share-card frames, Watch Game court floors (parquet, blonde maple, midnight, street) and GM titles.
**Daily goals:** three goals a day in any official GM league, the same for everyone, paying XP.
**Online weekly leaderboards** for the Rebuild of the Week and the Career of the Week.
**League codes:** send a code and a friend starts the exact same league (rosters, draft classes, schedule).
**Highlight GIFs** from Watch Game, ready for Discord.

sections.h2: Late September 2026: weekly challenges and the app

items: **Rebuild of the Week and Career of the Week:** a new shared challenge every Monday, the same league and the same wheel for everyone.
**Seven new Rebuild scenarios** (19 in all): the 11-71 Mavericks and Nuggets, the 12-70 Nets, Wade alone in Miami, Orlando after T-Mac, the 13-69 Hawks and the young Giannis Bucks.
**Install Court Vision** as an app on phones and computers. After the first visit it opens offline.
**Graphics setting** in the menu footer: Lite mode for older phones stops looping animations and blur and uses fewer simulation workers.
**What's new** popup once after each update.
**Rebuild Challenge:** 12 real rock-bottom teams (19 since the late-September update), a season limit, scores, stars and a board.

**Career Mode:** create a player on the wheel of NBA history or in MyPlayer and live his whole career, in today's league or any past draft. Hall of Fame, all-time Top 100, career moments, jersey retirements.
**League Hunt:** spin a six-man squad from all of history and win ten best-of-seven series against the great teams of every era. Daily Legend, decks, difficulty, Album and Dream Matchup.
**GM Locker:** every trophy you have won, across every mode.
**Backup everything:** one file with all your progress; restore on any device.
**Share cards:** pixel-art images of your results to post anywhere.
Trade Deadline Day, trade talks with counteroffers, three-team trades.
Agent negotiations, in-season extensions and contract years.
Draft Lottery and Draft Night war room; scouting department; Summer League.
Coaching carousel, staff roles and poaching, summer development camps.
Medical room with treatment decisions and load management.
Sideline coaching while you watch; your playoff series and Game 7s live.
Press conferences, storylines, franchise business (tickets, arena, merchandise) and the Year in Review show.
Real history: mid-season trades, real draft picks, real jersey numbers and every real player's career.
New arena and court look, team colors and logos, and a faster simulation engine.

pages.title: Contact CourtVision: support, bug reports and privacy help
pages.description: Get CourtVision support through the NineFoldVision Discord community. Learn what to include in a bug report and how to find save recovery and account deletion controls.
pages.lead: CourtVision is developed by NineFoldVision. The existing [Discord community](https://discord.gg/5uGK5HDS8e) is the published way to reach the developer, report problems and discuss the game. Discord is an external service and requires its own account to participate.

blocks.text: Describe the mode and action that failed, the result you expected and what actually happened. Include your browser, device and whether you were signed in or offline. Exact steps and an error screenshot are more useful than “it does not work.”

items: Note the season, round or screen where the problem happened.
Say whether it happens again after reopening the same save.
Never post passwords, sign-in links, account tokens or payment information. Backup files contain game data: review them and agree on an appropriate support channel before sharing.

blocks.text: Do not clear browser data when investigating a missing save. First check the same browser and profile, then look for save recovery points or a downloaded backup. The [FAQ](faq.html) explains the difference between local saves and cloud progress.

Account deletion is available from the account screen in Community. If it fails, report the error without sharing authentication details. Cancel any recurring Support Shop subscription before deleting the account.

Read the [Privacy Policy](privacy.html) for the data disclosures and controls. If you need help reaching the developer about a privacy request, use the Discord community to ask for an appropriate private contact route; do not post personal information in public channels. No response-time guarantee is made.

For a gameplay question, begin with the [FAQ](faq.html), [beginner guide](how-to-play.html) or [mode guides](guides/). When suggesting a change, explain the situation it would improve and which mode it affects. Keeping reports specific helps a solo developer reproduce and prioritize them.
